_comment: Dispositions for the TACTICAL migration set's outward calls (RI-TACT / TACT-CUT, 2026-08-25).
Consumed by tools/gen_migration.py --domain tact (--effects prints it; the manifest carries it
as _outward_effects) and by tools/gen_dll_effects.py, which generates one gate per entry. That
generator merges EVERY domain's dispositions into one header, because a gate is a hook over an
ADDRESS and two domains cannot each own one; it refuses a name two domains classify differently.
WHY EACH CLASS MATTERS. Shadow mode snapshots, runs the ORIGINAL, RESTORES the pre-state, runs
OURS, compares. A state restore does not un-play a sound, un-draw a pixel or un-write a file, so:
effectful -- performed in the ORIGINAL arm, SUPPRESSED in ours, RECORDED in both. Fires once.
pure      -- a query. Performed in BOTH arms and MUST NOT be suppressed. The seam's NEGATIVE
ARM: a suppression built only from the effectful cases passes its own test
vacuously. This domain has three, plus eleven `state`.
state     -- mutates state, but passes the twice-test below. Performed in both arms.
THE TEST THIS FILE APPLIES, and it is not the obvious one:
Is running this body TWICE, back to back, with the same inputs, observationally
different from running it once?
The obvious rule -- 'effectful only if it reaches present_flip or a device/COM/file API' -- was
proposed by the adversarial review and is WRONG on real bodies in this very set:
* llm_tact_scroll_fade_step calls NOTHING. Its body is load [EDI], mask, ADD 0x2 / 0x80 /
0x1000 with saturation, MOV word ptr [EDI],DX (@0x0043c38e) over every framebuffer pixel --
a read-modify-write BRIGHTEN. Twice = twice the fade, on a buffer nothing restores.
* llm_tact_drag_box_clamp's leaf stores constant dash pixels (idempotent) but ROLs the dash-
phase global once per pixel (`ROL byte ptr [0x0055992b],0x1` @0x0043ab30). Twice = a
different pattern.
* And the rule cuts the other way too: llm_tact_tile_overlay_refresh writes only constants,
in its body and in both of its leaves, so it is `state` despite drawing -- the first
reading called it effectful and was overturned here.
So: look for accumulators. A read-modify-write on anything, a rotating pattern register, a queue
consumed, a PRNG stepped, a running base offset, an in-place format conversion, a handle taken.
THE MEASUREMENT WAS SHORT, AND CLOSING THAT IS HALF OF WHAT THIS ITEM DID. The inventory counts
edges from the migration set into the domain's declared effect FAMILIES, and this domain's
families are its 56 named presentation walls -- every one of them a closure member by
construction. So calls out to SHARED, non-exclusive code were structurally invisible.
llm_ui_set_draw_surface is called from NINE tactical members; its body sets the blit globals and
then calls llm_gfx_blit_rect_rows, which memcpys rows into _G_LLM_GFX_DRAW_SURFACE. It drew, it
was in no gate list, and an armed site over any of those nine would have blitted twice with
every check green. `select.effect_names` in the domain profile now names such callees, and
gating that ONE convergence point is what lets llm_tact_ui_char_panel_ammo_draw stay `state` and
llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_refresh stay `pure` instead of marking nine ancestors effectful.
SUPPRESSION HAS ITS OWN FAILURE MODE, AND IT IS NOW CHECKED. `--effects` reports BLINDED WRITES:
every `effectful` target that writes a region carrying `hash` or `shadow`. Suppressing such a
target removes a write the comparison expected, so an armed call diverges because of the seam
rather than because of our code. Measured over these 31: exactly one, llm_tact_render_view
(_G_LLM_MAP_CAM_COL/_ROW), acknowledged in `_blinded_ack` below with its reason. That check is
the mirror of UNGATED REACH, which only ever guarded the opposite direction.
PROVEN ON THE RIG, BOTH DIRECTIONS, MUTATION-CHECKED. `test_ui.py --tact-effects-probe N` opens
one shadow window at tactical frame N over a real EFFECTFUL gate and a real non-effectful one
and requires performed=1/suppressed=1 and performed=2/suppressed=0 respectively. Absence of
either line is a FAIL, not a pass. Flipping the negative subject to `effectful` drops it to
performed=1 and the check names the over-refusal; flipping the effectful subject to `state`
raises it to performed=2 and the check names the double-fire.
A target with no entry here is reported UNCLASSIFIED; an entry naming a target nothing calls any
more is reported STALE. Both counts are printed even when zero.
FIELDS: class / verified / why / evidence_addr (the instruction the reading turns on) /
fake_return (what a suppressed call returns; every target here is void, so none needs one) /
note (traps for a later translator).
TACT-CUT2 (2026-08-27) ADDED THE 31 SHARED CALLEES, and the paragraph above explains why they
were invisible: effect membership is a name prefix or a named wall, and a wall is a closure
member by construction, so a call OUT of the closure matched neither half. `select.effect_names`
in the domain profile is the third half; these 31 names are what it holds. Their bodies were
classified and adversarially re-checked in tools/data/tact_shared_callees.json (13 effectful,
6 pure, 12 state; 31/31 verified, zero overturned), and the class carried here verbatim.
WHAT TACT-CUT2 ADDED ON TOP OF THE CARRY-OVER IS THE SECOND QUESTION, which the twice-test does
not ask: CAN THIS ENTRY ACTUALLY TAKE A GATE, AND CAN OUR ARM SURVIVE THE SUPPRESSION? FIVE
entries answered no. Each carries `gate: false` with its reason rather than being dropped -- a
hole somebody wrote down is a different object from a hole nobody noticed, and --effects prints
them under DELIBERATELY UNGATED on every run while the DLL logs one UNGATED ON PURPOSE line per
entry at install:
* llm_math_atan      -- its 9 stolen bytes are FLD + CALL rel32, and install_trampoline copies
stolen bytes VERBATIM. MEASURED: gating it sent every tactical atan to
a wrong address, the mission ended after frame 1, and the determinism
run reported '0 frames' with no crash dump.
* llm_rand           -- the same shape (PUSH EDX + CALL rel32), latent rather than observed.
NOT unmediated, though: the harness pin owns the entry and its
pinned_rand_next() calls mh::effects::enter_deferred().
* w_sprintf          -- __cdecl variadic; its proto is a derived one-call-site varargs SHAPE,
and a gate re-pushing only those params would corrupt 61 call sites.
* GetResourseFilePtr -- all four call sites dereference the returned buffer unguarded, so any
fake_return is an access violation, not a wrong answer.
* time_GetCurrentTime-- the harness pin owns the entry in every tactical rig run AND it is
`pure`, so the gate could only ever record -- into a 64-event window
log its 24 callers would overflow, disabling the INV-4 verdict.
THE FIRST TWO ARE NOW A MECHANICAL GATE RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT. tools/dump_steal_relbranch.py
asks Ghidra, for every function with a committed steal length, whether its stolen bytes contain
a pc-relative branch (18 of 2081 do); gen_dll_effects.py REFUSES to gate a flagged target and
refuses to run at all if a target it wants to gate is missing from that file. A byte scan cannot
do this job -- looking for 0xE8/0xE9 finds both real cases and also flags two long-working gates
whose byte 4 is part of a PUSH imm32 operand.
AN UNGATED TARGET STILL GETS A RECORD, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy: an owner that
honours the disposition from INSIDE its own replacement calls mh::effects::enter_deferred(addr),
which looks the record up. That is how llm_rand keeps exactly-once under the pin, proven on the
rig by the TACTPROBE shared-effectful line and mutation-checked in both directions.
AND SEVEN ENTRIES ALREADY HAD AN OWNER (C4, one owner per entry). The install order is what
makes that matter: reimpl_probe.cpp installs the gates before the sim shadow sites and the save
promotion, and net_seams.cpp installs them before video -- so the effects seam WINS every
contested entry unless it stands down. effects_install.cpp defers five of them on the SAME
mh_net.ini key the owner itself reads ([video] width/height, [video] picker, [promote] load,
[shadow] llm_strat_unit_remove_from_map, [shadow] llm_strat_unit_teardown), and each deferral
is logged BY OWNER NAME rather than counted. The sixth, time_GetCurrentTime, is ungated above.
The seventh is llm_rand, and it is the one a deferral could not fix: pin_rand replaces the body
with an LCG that STILL ADVANCES, so both arms would draw. It defers itself from harness.cpp
(its key lives in the [harness] section, not this one) and its pinned body calls
mh::effects::enter_deferred() -- the owner honouring the disposition from the inside.

llm_gfx_apply_resolution_change.why: Own body directly (not through any gated target) calls llm_ui_info_media_draw_p2() at entry, which itself calls llm_ui_widget_list_draw() -- a real screen draw -- and later calls llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution(w,h), whose depth-2 closure is MoveWindow/SetCapture/llm_gfx_release_display_surfaces/llm_gfx_ddraw_set_display_mode/llm_gfx_present_flip/llm_input_dimouse_shutdown: an actual OS window resize + DirectDraw surface teardown-and-recreate + present/flip + input-device release. None of that is undoable by a state restore, and llm_ui_info_media_draw_p2 / llm_tact_ui_sel_panel_free_gfx are both ungated (only p1 and sel_panel_draw are in the 31). Double-firing on an armed shadow call would resize/reflip the real window and redraw the info panel twice while the state diff reads clean. The function also resets several globals (_G_LLM_GFX_VIEW_TILE_HEIGHT_PX, the whole _G_LLM_BANK_SPRITE_BASE table, glyph pointers) but per the doctrine those ride along inside the single recorded effectful call -- reserving effectful is correct here since the irreversible act is the function's own direct job, not something delegated through another of the 31.

llm_gfx_load_all_sprite_banks.why: Own body (0x00465093, 41 bytes) is a bare 2-call sequencing wrapper: llm_gfx_load_sprite_bank_files() then llm_gfx_load_planet_extra_sprite_banks(). Read both callees' full bodies: each does GetResourseFilePtr (deterministic resource-file read) then a chain of REP MOVSD/MOVSB copies into global sprite-bank buffers (_G_LLM_GFX_BANK_PIXELS, _G_LLM_SPRITE_PIX_OFFSETS, _G_LLM_SPRITE_META, _G_LLM_GFX_BANK_PALETTES, _G_LLM_SPRITE_PAL_OFFSETS) plus utils_free and a call to llm_gfx_init_pixel_format (also read: pure loop recomputing palette words into _G_LLM_GFX_BANK_PALETTES_DARK plus a handful of scalar globals, zero calls). No blit, no DirectDraw, no sound anywhere in the closure -- this is a load-into-memory routine, restorable as a shadow region over the listed globals. The one UNGATED REACH hit (llm_gfx_load_sprite_bank_files, a wall not in this 31-name batch) is genuinely benign, not a sign the parent needs to be effectful.
llm_gfx_load_all_sprite_banks.note: llm_gfx_load_planet_extra_sprite_banks (the 2nd callee, not itself a wall so it never surfaced as an UNGATED REACH) has the identical shape -- also read in full via ReVa, same conclusion.

llm_snd_stop_all_channels.why: Own body loops over every sound channel and calls llm_snd_release_channel_voice(i) directly (CALL at 0x0042ef50) -- that callee is NOT one of the 31 gate-list targets, and it issues real DirectSound vtable calls (Stop at vtable+0x24, conditionally +0x48, then Release at vtable+8, read at 0x004d2714-0x004d2756 in the callee) on the channel's live IDirectSoundBuffer. That is an irreversible COM/audio-device action a state restore cannot undo. The function also zeroes each channel's retrigger-time bookkeeping (state), but since the irreversible reach lands on an UNGATED function rather than another of the 31, the doctrine's state-not-effectful exception does not apply -- this is a target whose own body performs (via a direct, non-gated call) the irreversible act.
llm_snd_stop_all_channels.note: llm_snd_release_channel_voice is a generic sound-engine internal shared by 7 callers across boot/menu/tactical (llm_game_boot_init, llm_ui_planet_select_screen_open, llm_ui_outcome_dlg_open, llm_game_return_to_main_menu_cb, etc.), not tactical-specific -- correctly outside the 31-name gate list rather than a gap in it.

llm_tact_blink_overlay_clear.why: Leaf function (calls only utils_assert_stack_capacity, a debug-build stack check, not a real callee). The only write is `MOV byte ptr [EAX + 0x713920],0x1` at 0x0042eda3, filling a 20x20 (400-byte) region of _G_LLM_TILE_DRAWN_MAP (0x00713920, byte[300+] per docs/symbols.md). docs/gfx-sprites.md documents this array as 'internal render-pipeline bookkeeping' stamped by the blitters -- ordinary heap/data-segment memory, not a pixel surface or any hardware-facing target. Fully shadow-region declarable and rollback-safe: no external effect.

llm_tact_drag_box_clamp.why: EFFECTFUL, against the review, and the deciding instruction is one the review did not look for. Its own body only clamps four rect globals -- that much of the overturn is right -- but it calls llm_gfx_draw_dashed_rect_outline (0x0043aa88), whose pixel stores are constants (idempotent) while its DASH PHASE is not: `ROL byte ptr [0x0055992b],0x1` at 0x0043ab30, 0x0043ab61, 0x0043ab96 and again on the fourth edge, once per dash pixel, with the value persisted in a global and reloaded next frame (MOV AL,[0x0055992b] @0x0043aaab). Running the outline twice leaves the marching-ants pattern at a different phase, and nothing restores DAT_0055992b. The review's rule -- effectful only if it reaches present_flip or a device API -- misses every accumulator of this kind.
llm_tact_drag_box_clamp.note: Params x1,y1,x2,y2 are window/screen-space pixel coords (compared against G_WIN_W/WindowHeight, not tile grid) -- plain int is correct, do NOT retype as map_t_tile_coord/fine_coord.

llm_tact_frame_cursor_and_reset.why: Own body performs two irreversible display acts directly, not through any gated target: CALL llm_gfx_draw_cursor_ingame at 0x0042964c (which conditionally blits the cursor sprite into the live framebuffer via llm_gfx_blit_sprite_rle), then unconditionally CALL llm_gfx_present_flip at 0x00429651 (the DirectDraw surface flip that actually pushes the framebuffer to the display -- the canonical 'un-drawable' act). Neither llm_gfx_draw_cursor_ingame nor llm_gfx_present_flip is in the 31-name gate list, so this reach is ungated and the parent itself must be effectful (doctrine case a). After the two calls the function also loops over _G_LLM_VIEW_TILES_W*_G_LLM_VIEW_TILES_H tiles clearing _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP's low bit and zeroing _G_LLM_TILE_DRAWN_MAP -- pure state bookkeeping, but it cannot be split from the irreversible calls that precede it in the same straight-line body, so the whole target is suppressed as one unit and the oracle is knowingly blind to that state slice for this target.
llm_tact_frame_cursor_and_reset.note: Params: none (void/void). No untyped struct pointers or enum opportunities in this body -- it's straight-line index math over already-named globals.

llm_tact_fx_play_sound.why: Body selects one of four output channels (2,3,4,5) by a retrigger-cooldown comparison and calls llm_snd_play_matching_sample (CALL at 0x0042f113/0x0042f161/0x0042f1c3/0x0042f211) -- not a gate-list target -- which on a name match calls llm_snd_channel_configure_voice_and_play (also ungated), whose body (read: DirectSound CreateSoundBuffer at vtable+0xc @0x004d2981, SetFrequency/SetPan @0x004d29cd/0x004d29ed, then the Lock/fill(FUN_0066efc9 memcpy)/Unlock/Play sequence @0x004d2a3e-0x004d2a7e) actually starts audio playback -- irreversible. The function also FSTPs the current time into four per-fx last-triggered timestamps (state), but the irreversible reach is through ungated helpers, so the state exception does not apply.
llm_tact_fx_play_sound.note: time_GetCurrentTime (also reached) is a pure clock read, not itself part of the effect chain -- listed for completeness only. FUN_0066efc9 is a plain memcpy-style buffer fill inside the Lock/Unlock window, not an unnamed device call itself, but it executes downstream of the real device calls so the whole chain is irreversible regardless.

llm_tact_gfx_load_banks_alt.why: Own body loads the alt sprite banks (100+, enemy-base interiors) the same way as llm_gfx_load_sprite_bank_files: GetResourseFilePtr + REP-MOVS copies into the shared global sprite-bank buffers, then conditionally calls gfx_TransformBankData on the just-copied pixel buffer and finishes with llm_gfx_init_pixel_format (already verified pure elsewhere in this family). Read gfx_TransformBankData's full body: it is a self-contained in-place RLE-aware byte-shuffle (5-5-5->5-6-5 recolor) of the same buffer, zero CALL instructions, no draw/sound/device access. No presentation or audio effect anywhere in the closure -- restorable as a shadow region over the sprite-bank globals.

llm_tact_gfx_view_tile_rows_init.why: Body (asm-confirmed, 4 CALLs total) does: CALL llm_gfx_view_metrics_init at 0x004294fb, own-body row-pointer-table writes (_G_LLM_TACT_VIEW_TILE_FB_ROW_PTRS store at 0x0042956b, _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP store at 0x0042957d), CALL game_SetEvent at 0x00429620 with the constant argument EAX=0xa loaded at 0x0042961b (=HUD_REDRAW_ALL), and CALL llm_map_cam_mark_viewport_dirty at 0x00429625. Read all three non-gated callees directly: llm_gfx_view_metrics_init (0x0044e150) contains no CALLs at all besides utils_assert_stack_capacity, only viewport-derived global arithmetic writes; llm_map_cam_mark_viewport_dirty (0x004a5a6b) likewise contains no CALLs, only a dirty-flag store and a memset-style loop over _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP; game_SetEvent's HUD_REDRAW_ALL case (decompile lines 106-109) is just `_G_LLM_STRAT_UI_PANEL_SWITCH_PENDING = 1; _G_LLM_STRAT_UI_VIEW_RESIZE_PENDING = 1;` with no calls -- the llm_snd_play/llm_ui_planet_select_screen_open calls the brief's depth-2/3 closure lists live in game_SetEvent's DIFFERENT ACTION_DENIED_FEEDBACK case (type=11), which this call site never reaches because it always passes the literal constant HUD_REDRAW_ALL (10). So every reachable path from this target is pure global-flag/pointer-table bookkeeping -- nothing irreversible ever fires, matching gen_migration.py reporting no ungated-irreversible finding.
llm_tact_gfx_view_tile_rows_init.note: llm_gfx_view_metrics_init and llm_tact_view_metrics_init are distinct sibling functions with near-identical names/roles (strategic-resize-triggered vs. tactical-mission-start pointer-table init) -- easy to conflate when skimming; worth double-checking any future doc cross-reference doesn't merge them.

llm_tact_mark_view_tiles_dirty.why: Leaf function, calls nothing (confirmed in the .asm -- no CALL instruction anywhere in the 0x20-byte body). It only does a REP STOSB memset loop writing 0x01 into a 20-row x 15-col region starting at [_G_LLM_TILE_DRAWN_MAP_PTR] (row stride 0x14=20, 0xf=15 bytes written per row, pad 5). That is a plain dirty-flag array write with no external effect at all -- it is the mechanism that makes the render pass redraw those tiles later, not a render/sound act itself.

llm_tact_render_view.why: Top-level per-frame scene renderer. Its OWN body directly calls irreversible draw primitives, not just via callees: CALL llm_gfx_draw_sprite_rle at 0x0042d504/0x0042d56d/0x0042d5d3/0x0042da7c/0x0042db1a/0x0042dd7f..0x0042ddcf (terrain tile overlay sprites, debug-stats sprite, mine-blast sprite, countdown-clock digit sprites), CALL llm_gfx_draw_sprite_v2 at 0x0042dc50 (fog-dimmed tile height sprites), CALL llm_gfx_sprite_clone_frame_pixels at 0x0042d824 and CALL llm_gfx_font_draw_glyph_solid at 0x0042d8cd/0x0042d92e/0x0042d99e/0x0042d9f0/0x0042da37 (debug overlay text). A second execution (armed original + our shadow both drawing) double-draws the frame -- state restore cannot undo a blit already written to the framebuffer/DirectDraw surface. Per doctrine this is the 'own body performs the irreversible act' case, so effectful is correct even though the function also does legitimate camera/vis-map state writes (_G_LLM_MAP_CAM_COL/ROW, _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP, _G_LLM_TILE_DRAWN_MAP, _G_LLM_TACT_HOVERED_UNIT_ID) -- those are accepted collateral of suppressing a genuinely effectful top-level renderer, not a reason to reclassify.
llm_tact_render_view.note: Reads a union arm (unit.tact.layers) per the plate's own 2026-08-24 note -- already correctly typed/commented, no further action needed. Suppressing the whole body in the shadow arm means these listed non-gated draw/entity leaves never fire in ours either, which is the intended effect since the parent itself is the effectful target.

llm_tact_save_screenshot.why: Body increments _G_LLM_TACT_SCREENSHOT_COUNTER, sprintf's a 'shot%04d.pcx' filename into a stack buffer, then CALLs llm_gfx_save_screenshot_rle at 0x00499f3a passing the live framebuffer pointer, draw-surface pointer and the filename. Read that callee's body: it builds a PCX header via utils_fill_data and (per the brief's depth-2 closure) calls utils_open_file/utils_write_to_file/utils_close_file -- a genuine disk write. llm_gfx_save_screenshot_rle is not in the gate list, so the reach is ungated and the parent is effectful (doctrine case a) -- a file write is definitionally something a state-restore snapshot cannot undo.
llm_tact_save_screenshot.note: llm_gfx_save_screenshot_rle's second param is unused (undefined4 unused_param2) per its own prototype comment -- a pre-existing observation, not something to act on here.

llm_tact_scroll_fade_step.why: EFFECTFUL, against the review, and this is the clearest case in the set. The function calls NOTHING -- it reaches no device API, no present, no COM, which is exactly why the review's rule cleared it. Its body is a READ-MODIFY-WRITE over every framebuffer pixel: load [EDI], mask each channel, `ADD EBX,0x2` @0x0043c342 / `ADD EBX,0x80` @0x0043c35c / `ADD EBX,0x1000` @0x0043c379 with saturation clamps, then `MOV word ptr [EDI],DX` @0x0043c38e. Running it twice brightens twice. The back-buffer is not a declared shadow region, so nothing restores it, and the frame is presented later regardless of who wrote it. A second execution is a visibly different frame.
llm_tact_scroll_fade_step.note: Decompile shows the __mh_watcall_ecx_ebx_volatile prototype with two unused undefined4 params passed straight through to an undefined8 return via CONCAT44 -- looks like leftover register content rather than real inputs/outputs (brief confirms the real signature is void(void), consistent with all 31 targets). Worth a todo:proto cleanup if this function is worked for real; not acted on here.

llm_tact_tile_overlay_refresh.why: STATE -- the review is right and the first reading was not. Every write here is an UNCONDITIONAL STORE OF A CONSTANT computed from values it only reads: 0xc618 / 0xfbef / 0x7bff into _G_LLM_TACT_UI_MINIMAP_OVERLAY_PTR, and both callees are the same shape -- llm_tact_ui_minimap_draw_viewport_outline stores 0xffff/0xffffffff along four edges, llm_tact_tile_clear_margin_patch stores 0x1f1f1f1f and 0x2020202 over a six-row margin. No accumulator anywhere in the subtree, so it passes the twice-test: running it twice leaves the overlay byte-for-byte identical. Reclassified rather than defended, because the rule this file applies to drag_box_clamp and scroll_fade_step has to cut both ways.
llm_tact_tile_overlay_refresh.note: The exported plate/decompile header still says 'return value passed to llm_tact_frame_cursor_and_reset' from an earlier partial read, but the function's real signature is void(void) (brief confirms all 31 targets are void) -- that plate line is stale and worth fixing when this function is next touched for real (not acted on here, read-only).

llm_tact_ui_char_panel_ammo_draw.why: STATE, and only because llm_ui_set_draw_surface is now a GATED TARGET (select.effect_names). The review was right that this body blits -- CALL llm_ui_set_draw_surface @0x00434212, which ends in llm_gfx_blit_rect_rows and memcpys rows into _G_LLM_GFX_DRAW_SURFACE -- and while that callee was ungated, `state` here would have double-blitted the ammo panel on every armed call. The fix is the one the gate design already implies: gate the shared convergence point once, not each of its nine tactical ancestors. With the gate there, this body's own writes are the tile-dirty flags (MOV byte ptr [DAT_00713d1e],0x2 @0x004342fc and @0x00434312) and its whole irreversible reach terminates at gates -- llm_ui_set_draw_surface and llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16 (@0x004342b4/@0x004342e8). Suppressing it instead would blind the oracle to the dirty flags for nothing.
llm_tact_ui_char_panel_ammo_draw.note: Also calls llm_gfx_pack_rgb16 (pure -- reads only G_COLOR_FORMAT per state_matrix.json, no writes), llm_str_ansi_to_wide_scratch (private scratch-buffer string conversion, no externally visible effect), and llm_ui_set_draw_surface (state_matrix.json shows it only writes clip/pointer/pitch config globals like _G_LLM_UI_SURFACE_PTR/_PITCH -- it configures the surface, it does not itself write pixels). None of these three are in the 31 but none perform an irreversible act either, so they are benign and don't constitute an ungated reach.

llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_refresh.why: PURE, for the same reason ammo_draw is now state: the review's overturn to `effectful` was correct against the gate list AS IT STOOD, since llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_draw calls llm_ui_set_draw_surface directly at 0x00434384 and that was ungated. It is gated now. This body itself writes NOTHING -- it reads _G_LLM_TACT_UI_SEL_PANEL_MULTI_MODE, DAT_00559098, _G_LLM_TACT_SIDEBAR_SLOT_SCROLL and the slot-id array into stack locals to find a row, then makes one conditional CALL at 0x00434f85. Zero stores, so neither `state` nor `effectful` describes it, and it is one of the three targets that give the seam a real negative arm.
llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_refresh.note: llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_draw (0x00434322, not in the 31) is the intermediate hop -- verified by reading its .c: it writes _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP_M6 state itself and calls llm_ui_set_draw_surface (benign config, see sibling row) but every draw call it makes lands on a gate-list target, so it introduces no ungated reach for this target.

llm_tact_ui_draw_player_row_list.why: Body calls llm_ui_set_draw_surface directly (CALL 0x004a8b73 at 0x00435545 and 0x0043560e, once per branch of the per-row highlight/no-highlight split) for the row-highlight icon blit, in addition to calling the gated llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16 (CALL 0x0041be9d at 0x0043559f/0x004355d3) for the row label text. GetResourseFilePtr.why: The resource-load entry point: rsr_GetFileEntry(fileName) locates the pack entry, then the body does CALL file_seek (0x004cf0a9, repositions the pack's shared file handle), CALL utils_malloc (0x004cf0b4, fresh heap allocation), CALL utils_read_from_file (0x004cf0e1, real disk I/O into that buffer), and on an 'LZW' magic match a second CALL utils_malloc (0x004cf110) + CALL LZW_Decompress (0x004cf12a) + CALL utils_free (0x004cf135) of the first buffer.
GetResourseFilePtr.evidence_addr: 0x004cf0a9 (CALL file_seek -- first irreversible action) and 0x004cf0e1 (CALL utils_read_from_file -- the actual disk read)
GetResourseFilePtr.twice_test: YES, differs. Two back-to-back calls perform two file seeks + two disk reads and hand back two DISTINCT freshly-malloc'd buffers (plus, on the LZW path, a second decompress + a second free of a different allocation) -- exactly the doctrine's 'a file opened or written' / 'a handle allocated' / 'memory freed' trigger list, not a restorable pure computation.
GetResourseFilePtr.gate_why: SUPPRESSION IS AN ACCESS VIOLATION HERE, not a wrong answer. It returns a freshly loaded resource buffer and ALL FOUR of its tactical call sites dereference the result with no NULL guard: llm_tact_ui_sel_panel_init stores it into _G_LLM_TACT_SEL_PANEL_ICON_GFX and reads the sprite header at 0x00433f24/0x00433f55/0x00433f89; llm_tact_mission_load parses the POZ text buffer byte-by-byte (0x00437454), memcpys the MAP buffer (0x004376fe) and hands the GROUND buffer to llm_tlo_palette_convert_565_to_555, which read-modify-writes it 255 times from 0x0043c7cc. `state`/`pure` are no better: its irreversible leaves are a seek on the shared pack handle (0x004cf0a9) and utils_malloc/utils_free churn (0x004cf0b4, 0x004cf110, 0x004cf135), and NO declared region covers either -- the region named `file_ptr` is a different global (0x00520469, the ground/TLO palette pointer), not the pack handle. Performing it in both arms leaks the GROUND buffer every window, since only one of the two pointers survives the restore and nothing frees the other. So its callers are structurally un-shadow-armable and are proven OFFLINE instead, which is already what llm_tact_mission_load's ledger row records.
GetResourseFilePtr.call_sites_correction: tact_shared_callees.json records call_sites: 2 (one per caller). The real count is 4 -- llm_tact_mission_load calls it three times (POZ text 0x00437454, MAP 0x004376fe, GROUND 0x004379e8). Recorded here rather than silently fixed upstream because a future reader computing the consequence of suppression from that field would miss two sites.

gfx_LoadSprite.why: Body is four unconditional stores driven purely by the `id` parameter: sprite_data (0x0042655d, bank-pixels base + per-id offset), _G_LLM_CURSOR_PALETTE (0x00426577, bank-palettes base + per-id offset), _G_LLM_CURSOR_HOTSPOT_X (0x00426588, sprite-meta[id].origin_x), _G_LLM_CURSOR_HOTSPOT_Y (0x00426598, sprite-meta[id].origin_y). It calls nothing else (only utils_assert_stack_capacity) -- no draw, no blit, purely a cursor/sprite-pointer latch.
gfx_LoadSprite.evidence_addr: 0x00426598 (final MOV [_G_LLM_CURSOR_HOTSPOT_Y],EAX); 0x004265a6 (RET) confirms the body ends there with no further effect

llm_fatal_cleanup.why: Sets _G_LLM_GAME_MODE=0, then unconditionally calls a fixed sequence of teardown/shutdown functions: CoUninitialize (device/COM call at 0x0042615a), llm_gfx_free_draw_buffers, llm_gfx_planet_bank_free, FreeGlobalData, llm_strat_pathfinder_shutdown, llm_input_dimouse_shutdown, llm_input_di_keyboard_destroy, llm_gfx_font_unload/free_polalfa, llm_snd_shutdown, llm_gfx_release_display_surfaces, llm_net_shutdown_stub, and finally llm_game_clear_save_temp_files (deletes files) at 0x004261ac -- called immediately before utils::abort(0).
llm_fatal_cleanup.twice_test: YES, catastrophically. This is a one-shot process-fatal teardown: CoUninitialize a second time on an already-uninitialized COM apartment, freeing already-freed graphics/font/sound resources, releasing already-released DirectDraw surfaces, and re-deleting already-deleted save temp files are all real double-free/double-teardown hazards -- the doctrine's own framing ('un-play a sound... un-write a file') applies directly to llm_game_clear_save_temp_files and to the DirectSound/DirectDraw teardown calls.

llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution.why: Full OS-visible video-mode teardown/recreate: CALL llm_input_dimouse_shutdown (0x00428a2c), CALL llm_gfx_release_display_surfaces (0x00428a31, drops DirectDraw surfaces), CALL llm_gfx_set_window_resolution (0x00428a3c), then a real Win32 CALL dword ptr CS:[MoveWindow] on the game's hWnd for one of three fixed resolution branches (0x00428a60 / 0x00428a88 / 0x00428ab0), CALL llm_gfx_display_init (0x00428ac2), CALL SetCapture (0x00428acd, re-grabs the physical mouse), and CALL llm_map_cam_mark_viewport_dirty (0x00428ad4).
llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution.evidence_addr: 0x00428a60 (CALL dword ptr CS:[MoveWindow] -- real Win32 window resize) with corroborating irreversible calls at 0x00428a2c (dimouse_shutdown) and 0x00428acd (SetCapture)
llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution.twice_test: YES, differs. Calling this twice tears down and recreates the DirectDraw display surfaces and the OS window/mouse-capture state twice (a second MoveWindow + a second SetCapture + a second surface release/recreate cycle), which is player-visible (flicker, focus/capture churn) even when width/height are identical between the two calls -- exactly the doctrine's explicit 'a window resized' trigger, and this project's own D13 comment independently calls the whole release..recreate span 'unsafe to run a frame in'.
llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution.suppression_note: SUPPRESSION STARVES THE CALLER PARTIALLY, and it stays effectful anyway. Its callee llm_gfx_set_window_resolution (CALL at 0x00428a3c) sets G_COLOR_FORMAT, which is the run/skip guard both 565->555 converters read -- so a suppressed call changes what they do. But the same body performs MoveWindow/SetCapture and a DirectDraw surface teardown-and-recreate, which no restore undoes, so `state` is not available: the honest position is that a caller of this function cannot be shadow-armed at all. (The width/height writes themselves are safe -- llm_tact_mission_start re-hardcodes both immediately after the call.)
llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution.note: Entry conditionally owned by seams/video.cpp's D13 re-entrancy guard (install_reentrancy_guard, an install_trampoline detour), which is armed only by [video] width/height or [video] picker -- both default 0 and both unset in every rig path. effects_install.cpp defers the gate in exactly that configuration. The deferral is WEAKER than the promotion-shaped ones and deliberately says so: video's detour WRAPS the original rather than replacing it, so it performs the effect once per arm just as an ungated entry would. Operational rule: do not run a tactical shadow session over llm_tact_mission_start with those [video] keys set.

llm_gfx_convert_pixels_565_to_555.why: In-place RGB565->RGB555 squeeze over the caller's sprite_blob pixel array: for every pixel it reads *local_24 (MOVSX at 0x0043c84e), computes ((v&0xffc0)>>1)+(v&0x1f), and writes the result back into the SAME slot (0x0043c873) before advancing the pointer. The write target is also the read source of the transform, so the transform is applied to its own prior output on a repeat call.
llm_gfx_convert_pixels_565_to_555.evidence_addr: 0x0043c873 (MOV word ptr [EDX],AX -- the accumulating store back into the pixel just read at 0x0043c84e)
llm_gfx_convert_pixels_565_to_555.twice_test: YES, differs. First call converts real RGB565 data to RGB555 once. A back-to-back second call on the same buffer treats the already-squeezed RGB555 bits as if they were still RGB565 and reapplies the same shift/mask, producing garbage pixel values different from a single conversion -- structurally identical to the doctrine's brighten-RMW example, just for this format instead of the framebuffer.
llm_gfx_convert_pixels_565_to_555.suppression_note: SUPPRESSION STARVES THE CALLER. The body is a pure in-place read-modify-write over the sprite blob passed in (MOV word ptr [EDX],AX at 0x0043c873), and both tactical callers store that same pointer into a persistent array (_G_LLM_TACT_SEL_PANEL_ICON_GFX, _G_LLM_TACT_CHAR_PANEL_GFX) that every later frame blits from. NOT convertible to `state`: the buffer is heap memory whose size comes from the blob's own header, and a shadow region is a fixed base+size -- there is nothing to declare. So it stays effectful and its callers are OFFLINE rows.

llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb.why: Own body sets position/color globals then unconditionally calls llm_gfx_font_draw_glyph_blend_clipped (0x004a2d08 -> 0x004a2fdc), which I decompiled fully: for each covered glyph pixel it reads the CURRENT destination pixel byte (`(char)*psVar14` at 0x004a30ba, used as a LUT index alongside the source coverage/color) and writes the LUT-blended result back into that same destination pixel (0x004a30de). That is a genuine alpha-blend read-modify-write against the framebuffer, not a plain overwrite.
llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb.evidence_addr: 0x004a30b0/0x004a30ba (MOVZX reads of the existing dest pixel byte) and 0x004a30de (MOV word ptr [EDI],BX -- write of the blended value back into that same dest pixel), inside llm_gfx_font_draw_glyph_blend_clipped
llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb.twice_test: The accumulator is the destination pixel itself: blend(dst) = LUT_A[f(dst_lo)] + LUT_B[f(dst_hi,color)], then dst := blend(dst). Running the glyph draw twice back-to-back re-reads the ALREADY-BLENDED pixel as the new 'dst' input on pass two, producing a different (typically further-blended/darker) color than a single pass -- observably different from running it once. Classic non-idempotent alpha-blend RMW, same shape as the doctrine's dashed-outline phase-rotate example.

llm_gfx_font_select.why: Body is four unconditional stores driven purely by the font_slot parameter: _G_LLM_GFX_FONT_LINE_HEIGHT (0x004a2544, table lookup by slot), _G_LLM_GFX_CUR_FONT_GLYPH_PTR_TABLE (0x004a2555, table lookup by slot), and DAT_005d81f4 set to one of two fixed constant addresses depending on a slot<1 branch (0x004a2560 / 0x004a256c). No prior value of any of these globals is read before being overwritten.
llm_gfx_font_select.evidence_addr: 0x004a2544 (MOV [_G_LLM_GFX_FONT_LINE_HEIGHT],EAX) representative of all four stores; 0x004a257f (RET) confirms no further side effects
llm_gfx_font_select.twice_test: Every store is `global = f(font_slot)` with no term depending on the global's own prior value -- calling with the same font_slot twice writes the same four values both times. Passes the twice-test; this is config-latching, not accumulation.

llm_gfx_pack_rgb16.why: Full body is register/stack-local arithmetic: reads global G_COLOR_FORMAT once (0x0043c58a CMP against RGB555) to pick a shift/mask formula over the three byte params, stores the packed value into a local (EBP-0x10), and returns it in EAX. No global or shared memory is ever written -- every MOV target in the disassembly (0x0043c581/84/87/bd/e9) is a stack slot ([EBP+...]), not a DAT_/G_ symbol.
llm_gfx_pack_rgb16.evidence_addr: 0x0043c5f6 (RET) -- body between entry and RET contains zero writes to any address outside the local frame
llm_gfx_pack_rgb16.twice_test: No writes to shared state at all, so there is nothing for a second call to observe differently; a query in the strictest sense. Same inputs always produce the same return value with zero side effects.

llm_gfx_sprite_pix_offsets_init.why: Computes a single base address puVar1 = _G_LLM_SPRITE_PIX_OFFSETS[0] + _G_LLM_GFX_BANK_PIXELS (both globals it only READS, at 0x0049aca5/0x0049acaa) and then unconditionally stores 8 hardcoded word constants (1,1,1,1,1,1,1,0xffff) into puVar1[0..7] (0x0049acb8..0x0049acf6). llm_gfx_sprite_pix_offsets_init.evidence_addr: 0x0049acb8 (first constant store MOV word ptr [EAX],0x1) through 0x0049acf6 (last, MOV word ptr [EAX+0xe],0xffff)
llm_gfx_sprite_pix_offsets_init.twice_test: NO difference. The base address is recomputed identically from the two input globals each call, and the same 8 literal constants are written to it; a second call overwrites the slot with byte-identical values.

llm_gfx_view_metrics_init.why: Recomputes ~14 globals (G_WIN_W/H, _G_LLM_FB_PITCH, _G_LLM_VIEW_TILES_W/H, _G_LLM_VIEW_RADIUS_W/H, DAT_00825044/48/50, _G_LLM_GFX_PANEL_ROW_SKIP, _G_LLM_GFX_VIEWPORT_ROW_BYTES, and 5 fixed plane-pointer globals) purely as arithmetic over WindowWidth (0x005202c8) and WindowHeight (0x005202cc), which it only reads, plus one intra-function reuse of values it just computed in the same call (G_WIN_W read back at 0x0044e1a8/0x0044e1ad after being stored at 0x0044e172 -- consistent within one invocation, not an accumulator across invocations). Read the full asm: no field is ever read-modified against its own value from a PRIOR call.
llm_gfx_view_metrics_init.evidence_addr: 0x0044e172 (MOV [G_WIN_W],EAX -- first of 14 unconditional stores, all likewise fed only by WindowWidth/WindowHeight); ret at 0x0044e289
llm_gfx_view_metrics_init.twice_test: NO difference. With the same WindowWidth/WindowHeight inputs, every one of the 14 destination globals gets the same byte-identical value on call 2 as on call 1 -- confirmed by walking the whole asm body, since every store traces back to WindowWidth/WindowHeight/_G_LLM_GFX_VIEW_TILE_HEIGHT_PX, never to the destination global's own prior contents.

llm_input_key_dequeue.why: On queue non-empty, copies 14 bytes (MOVSD.REP, 0x004d1058) from the ring slot into the caller's buffer, then increments and wraps _G_LLM_INPUT_KEY_READ_IDX (INC/AND 0x7f, stored at 0x004d1063) -- a queue-advance, i.e. consumes one entry.
llm_input_key_dequeue.twice_test: YES -- consumes the queue's read index. Two back-to-back calls with the same starting state pop two DIFFERENT entries (or the second is a no-op if the queue only had one), versus one call popping one entry once -- observably different.
llm_input_key_dequeue.suppression_note: SUPPRESSION STARVES THE CALLER, and this one is an OUT-PARAMETER: the body memcpys a 0x38-byte ring slot into param_1 (REP MOVSD at 0x004d1058) and advances _G_LLM_INPUT_KEY_READ_IDX, and llm_tact_frame reads the out-buffer on the very next line. This is the one that COULD become `state` -- the ring and the read index are both at fixed addresses -- but _G_LLM_INPUT_KEY_EVENTS (0xe68110, 7168 B) and _G_LLM_INPUT_KEY_READ_IDX (0xe69dac) carry the `view` manifest and NOT `shadow`, so nothing restores them between arms today. Adding `shadow` to both is the change that would make it `state`; until then the pop is a real queue consumption and effectful is the honest class. Moot for the tactical caller in any case: llm_tact_frame's entry is owned by the tactical cadence hook, so no shadow window ever opens over it.

llm_input_key_queue_empty.why: Reads _G_LLM_INPUT_KEY_WRITE_IDX (0x00e69db4) and _G_LLM_INPUT_KEY_READ_IDX (0x00e69dac), compares them, returns a bool via SETZ. No memory writes anywhere in the 0x18-byte body.
llm_input_key_queue_empty.twice_test: NO -- pure comparison of two indices it does not modify; identical inputs (nothing else runs between the two calls) produce identical output both times.

llm_input_mouse_buttons_get.why: Body is just MOV EAX,[0x00824fbc] (a cached button-state mirror written by llm_input_mouse_delta_pump) followed by epilogue/RET. No writes anywhere.
llm_input_mouse_buttons_get.twice_test: NO -- pure read of a global that nothing in this function's own body writes; repeated calls (with no intervening writer) return the same value.

llm_input_mouse_delta_pump.why: Body accumulates into _G_LLM_INPUT_MOUSE_DELTA_X/Y (ADD dword ptr [0x005204d5]/[0x005204d9], 0x004266ce/0x004266d4/0x004266f2/0x004266f8) and drains the mouse event queue in a while(!empty) loop (CALL llm_input_mouse_queue_is_empty @0x00426699, CALL llm_input_mouse_pop_event @0x004266a5) -- a real queue consumer, not idempotent. Overwrites cursor globals _G_LLM_CURSOR_X/Y each iteration and per src/mh_dll/mh/seams/video.cpp:1173 also re-warps the OS cursor via SetCursorPos on frames the OS cursor is hidden.
llm_input_mouse_delta_pump.twice_test: YES -- the mouse event queue is a real accumulator (llm_input_mouse_queue_is_empty/llm_input_mouse_pop_event). First call drains it to empty and produces nonzero deltas; an immediate second call finds the queue already empty and produces zero deltas -- observably different from running once.
llm_input_mouse_delta_pump.suppression_note: SUPPRESSION STARVES THE CALLER. It writes _G_LLM_INPUT_MOUSE_DELTA_X/Y and _G_LLM_CURSOR_X/Y, and llm_tact_frame computes the camera-scroll branch straight off _G_LLM_CURSOR_X immediately after the call at 0x0042a0c9. Stays effectful because the body also reaches a real SetCursorPos, which no restore undoes, and because all four globals are `view`-only -- not in the `shadow` manifest. Same mootness as above for the tactical caller: llm_tact_frame cannot be armed.

llm_math_atan.why: Entire body is FLD double ptr [ESP+4]; CALL IF@ATAN (the Watcom FPU/CRT atan helper); RET 0x8 -- a thin wrapper around a pure math library routine. No memory writes.
llm_math_atan.twice_test: NO -- pure mathematical function of its float argument (atan); identical argument gives identical result every call, no state touched.
llm_math_atan.gate_why: ITS STOLEN BYTES CONTAIN A CALL rel32, SO A TRAMPOLINE OVER IT IS CORRUPT. llm_math_atan is 12 bytes at 0x004daa52 and its committed steal length is 9: `FLD qword ptr [ESP+4]` (4 bytes) followed by `CALL 0x004daa28` (5). mh::hook::install_trampoline copies the stolen bytes VERBATIM into a fresh allocation and relocates nothing, so the copied CALL branches by the original displacement from the new address -- somewhere arbitrary. MEASURED, not feared: gating it made llm_tact_calc_dir24's every atan leave the program, the tactical mission ended after frame 1, and `--tact-determinism` reported '0 frames' with NO crash dump -- a verdict that reads like a scenario problem and says nothing about a hook. Bisected to this one target on 2026-08-27. The class is `pure`, so nothing is lost: a gate would never have suppressed it, and its only contribution would have been INV-4 recording. tools/dump_steal_relbranch.py now measures this property for every proto in Ghidra and gen_dll_effects.py refuses to gate a flagged target (and refuses to run at all if one is missing from that file).

llm_rand.why: Classic Watcom CRT rand(): dereferences the seed pointer from FUN_004da981, computes seed*0x41c64e6d+0x3039 (IMUL/ADD at 0x00426995... i.e. 0x004da995/0x004da99b), stores the new seed back (0x004da9a1), and returns bits shifted/masked from it. An accumulating LCG state store.
llm_rand.twice_test: YES -- textbook PRNG: the seed store at 0x004da9a1 makes the second call return a different value than the first (or than repeating the first return) since the internal state advanced.
llm_rand.note: ENTRY OWNED BY THE HARNESS PIN, WHICH NOW ASKS THE SEAM ITSELF (TACT-CUT2). `pin_rand=1` is written into every tactical rig ini and MH_Harness_Init installs its LCG over llm_rand's entry before MH_Seam_Init reaches the gates, so an unconditional gate would fail its entry-byte guard and report PARTIALLY ARMED on every tactical run. harness.cpp therefore calls defer_entry() at its arm site AND pinned_rand_next() calls mh::effects::enter_deferred(), honouring the disposition from inside the owning mechanism -- because a bare deferral would only silence the report: the pin's LCG advances in BOTH arms, so the double draw the classification is about would still happen. fake_return 0 is inside rand()'s legal [0,0x7fff] and is deliberately neither the pinned seed (12345) nor the maximum, so it cannot be mistaken for a real draw. SUPPRESSION DOES NOT MAKE A RAND-DEPENDENT BODY ARMABLE -- the original arm draws a real value and ours gets 0, so the two diverge by construction; what it buys is that the game's PRNG advances ONCE per shadowed call instead of twice, which is what stopped a seam artefact from surfacing later as an unrelated sim divergence. Rows whose behaviour depends on a draw are OFFLINE rows.
llm_rand.gate_why: SAME TRAMPOLINE HAZARD AS llm_math_atan, and it was latent rather than observed. llm_rand's steal length is 6 and those bytes are `PUSH EDX` + `CALL 0x004da981` (the per-thread CRT data lookup) -- an unrelocatable rel32, so a gate here would have corrupted every draw the first time anyone ran with `pin_rand=0`. Under `pin_rand=1`, which tools/test_ui.py writes into EVERY tactical ini, no gate would have installed anyway: the harness LCG already owns this entry. BEING UNGATED DOES NOT MEAN UNMEDIATED HERE, and that is the point of the record this entry still gets: seams/harness.cpp's pinned_rand_next() calls mh::effects::enter_deferred() and honours the answer, so under the pin the draw happens in the ORIGINAL arm and is suppressed in ours -- proven on the rig by the TACTPROBE shared-effectful line (performed=1 suppressed=1), and mutation-checked both ways. THE RESIDUAL GAP, stated plainly: with `pin_rand=0` there is neither a gate nor a pin, so a shadow window over any of the six tactical callers would draw twice and shift the PRNG. No rig path sets it to 0; if one ever does, that run cannot be read as evidence about a rand-dependent body.

llm_snd_ambient_reseed_planet_event_time.why: Loop of 20 iterations, each computing a delay via utils_math_trunc then CALL llm_rand_below_fx at 0x0045e2d7, storing the draw into events[i].next_time via FSTP at 0x0045e2f2 (next_time = rand_draw + current_time).
llm_snd_ambient_reseed_planet_event_time.twice_test: YES, differently. llm_rand_below_fx draws from and ADVANCES the strategic PRNG (_G_LLM_STRAT_RNG_STATE slot 1 per src/mh_dll/mh_harness/harness.cpp's rng-slot table, and src/mh_dll/libmh/sim/sim_fx_debris_burst.h explicitly flags this as a 'SHADOW HAZARD: llm_rand_below_fx ADVANCES _G_LLM_STRAT_RNG_STATE INSIDE A CALLEE'). llm_rand_below_fx is a different function/address (0x00499f84) from the gate-listed llm_rand (0x004da98b), so its PRNG advance is NOT suppressed by any existing gate. A 2nd call draws 20 fresh (different) random numbers and overwrites next_time with different values, and leaves the PRNG state advanced by 20 more draws than a single run would.
llm_snd_ambient_reseed_planet_event_time.suppression_note: SUPPRESSION STARVES THE CALLER THROUGH THE RNG CHANNEL. The body burns twenty draws of llm_rand_below_fx (CALL at 0x0045e2d7) against _G_LLM_STRAT_RNG_STATE while filling _G_LLM_SND_AMBIENT_BY_PLANET[...].events[i].next_time, so a suppressed call leaves our arm twenty draws behind the original's -- a divergence that surfaces downstream rather than here. _G_LLM_STRAT_RNG_STATE IS a shadow region, but the ambient table is not, so `state` would fix half of it. Its only caller, llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic, is already recorded un-armable and proven OFFLINE, so the conclusion does not change -- only the reason on record does.

llm_snd_play_matching_sample.why: Scans a 0x2c-stride sound-slot table with strncmp (CALL 0x004e14c0 at 0x004d2b8e) and on a name match dispatches to CALL llm_snd_channel_configure_voice_and_play at 0x004d2ba8.
llm_snd_play_matching_sample.twice_test: YES, differently -- this is the exact case doctrine's own comment block calls out (src/mh_dll/mh/addr/mh_effects.gen.h, around the llm_tact_fx_play_sound / llm_tact_zone_sound_play entries): llm_snd_channel_configure_voice_and_play's body does a real DirectSound CreateSoundBuffer + Lock/fill/Unlock/Play sequence -- starting audio playback is irreversible and running it twice plays the sample twice (or restarts it). mh_effects.gen.h explicitly documents llm_snd_play_matching_sample as 'not a gate-list target' reaching this ungated DirectSound Play, confirming no existing suppression covers it.

llm_str_ansi_to_wide_scratch.why: Null-check then unconditional CALL (0x004cf412) to llm_str_ansi_to_wide(dst=&DAT_00660d24, src), which I decompiled: it strlen's src, calls Win32 MultiByteToWideChar(src,len,dst,len) to write the converted wide string into dst, then NUL-terminates dst[len]. All writes into the shared scratch buffer DAT_00660d24 are a pure function of the src string's bytes -- no counter, no queue, nothing read from the buffer before being overwritten.
llm_str_ansi_to_wide_scratch.evidence_addr: 0x004cf412 (CALL llm_str_ansi_to_wide) in llm_str_ansi_to_wide_scratch; inside the callee, 0x004cf3ba (CALL MultiByteToWideChar, the write) and 0x004cf3c9 (MOV word ptr [dst+len],0 -- NUL terminator)
llm_str_ansi_to_wide_scratch.twice_test: Given the same src pointer/content, the strlen, the MultiByteToWideChar conversion, and the NUL terminator all reproduce byte-identical output into DAT_00660d24 on a second call -- the scratch buffer's prior contents are never read, only overwritten. Passes the twice-test cleanly.

llm_strat_time_resync_and_tick.why: Body: CALL llm_time_get_ticks_ms (return value discarded) at 0x00449e39; CALL time_GetCurrentTime at 0x00449e3e; FSTP double ptr [LAST_GAME_TIME] at 0x00449e43 (unconditional overwrite, not an accumulator); CALL llm_strat_time_tick at 0x00449e49.

The remaining callee, llm_strat_time_tick, is itself a separately promoted/gated RI-LOCKSTEP target (libmh/lockstep/timekeeper.cpp, MH_EXPORT_REPLACE_llm_strat_time_tick, mh_patches.gen.h entry) -- per doctrine's exception, an irreversible/mixed effect reached through an already-gated target does not make the PARENT effectful.

llm_strat_unit_remove_from_map.why: Body has unconditional accumulator stores on the non-crewed-unit branch: ADD dword ptr [EAX+0xc3a37c],EDX (_G_LLM_STRAT_POP_STATS[player].human += Unit[proto].human) at 0x00487390, immediately followed by SUB dword ptr [EAX+0xc3a378],EDX (human_in_field -= same) at 0x004873c3, then a CALL to llm_strat_population_remove at 0x004873f3. The crewed-unit branch also DECs a live soldier-list counter (DEC word ptr [EAX+0xe0e5a8] at 0x004872ec) once per linked soldier.
llm_strat_unit_remove_from_map.twice_test: YES, differently. After call #1, units[player][idx].unit_id/.player are zeroed but unit_proto_id (the field the branch reads) is untouched, so a 2nd call re-enters the SAME non-crewed branch and re-applies human += / human_in_field -= and re-calls llm_strat_population_remove -- i.e. the population accumulator is double-counted. Also llm_strat_fow_remove_sight (0x00487265 call site 0x004874b7) is a real per-tile sight-count decrement callee, invoked unconditionally both times.
llm_strat_unit_remove_from_map.note: Entry conditionally owned by the RI-SIM shadow site ([shadow] llm_strat_unit_remove_from_map, default 0); effects_install.cpp defers the gate on that key. Polarity is the opposite of the lockstep precedent -- the owner is OFF by default, so ordinarily the gate installs and the live tactical call from llm_tact_squad_assault_resolve is covered. The sim domain does not classify this target, so gen_dll_effects' cross-domain merge has nothing to disagree with.

llm_strat_unit_teardown.why: Body has multiple unconditional accumulator decrements by unit category: DEC dword ptr [EAX+0xc38530] (used_vehicles -= 1) at 0x00487ce6, DEC dword ptr [EAX+0xc3853c] (used_planes -= 1) at 0x00487cf5, DEC dword ptr [EAX+0xc38538] (used_helis -= 1) at 0x00487d04, SUB dword ptr [EAX+0xc38534],EDX (used_soldiers -= soldier_count) at 0x00487d3c, plus a units_alive[planet] DEC at 0x00487f13 and a slot-[0].energy += HQ_ENERGY_CREDIT store.
llm_strat_unit_teardown.twice_test: YES, differently. Every housing counter (_G_LLM_STRAT_UNIT_HOUSING_STATS.used_*), units_alive[planet], and the HQ energy credit are decremented/incremented unconditionally on each call with no re-entrancy guard tied to whether the unit was already torn down -- a 2nd call double-decrements housing/units_alive and double-credits HQ energy, and (if units_alive hits 0 the first time) would call llm_strat_player_presence_lost again on the 2nd call too.
llm_strat_unit_teardown.note: Entry conditionally owned by the RI-SIM shadow site ([shadow] llm_strat_unit_teardown, default 0); same shape and same reasoning as llm_strat_unit_remove_from_map. EVIDENCE CORRECTION carried from the TACT-CUT2 verify stage: the HQ energy credit listed among its irreversible writes IS idempotent (guarded by unit.energy > 0 and zeroed in the same branch). The `effectful` verdict rests on the housing-counter decrements and units_alive alone.

llm_tact_vis_map_fill_default.why: Nested loop that STOSBs the constant byte 2 across the entire _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP_PTR grid (_G_LLM_VIEW_TILES_W x _G_LLM_VIEW_TILES_H): `STOSB ES:EDI` at 0x0043ac17, writing 2 unconditionally into every cell.
llm_tact_vis_map_fill_default.twice_test: NO -- every write is the same constant (2) into the same fixed grid, computed from no input other than the fixed grid geometry; identical to doctrine's own worked example of llm_tact_tile_overlay_refresh (constant fill, no accumulator). Running it twice leaves the grid identical to running it once.

llm_tlo_palette_convert_565_to_555.why: Same RGB565->RGB555 RMW squeeze as llm_gfx_convert_pixels_565_to_555, but over the global TLO palette buffer pointed to by `file_ptr` (0x00520469), entries 0..254: reads *local_1c (MOVSX at 0x0043c7cc), computes the shifted/masked value, and writes it back into the same slot at 0x0043c7f1 before incrementing.
llm_tlo_palette_convert_565_to_555.evidence_addr: 0x0043c7f1 (MOV word ptr [EDX],AX -- accumulating store back into the palette entry just read at 0x0043c7cc)
llm_tlo_palette_convert_565_to_555.twice_test: YES, differs. Identical failure mode to the sprite-pixel sibling: a second back-to-back call reconverts already-555-squeezed palette entries as if they were still 565, mangling the palette. No per-entry "already converted" guard exists -- only the one-time G_COLOR_FORMAT check gates whether the function runs at all, not whether it has already run.
llm_tlo_palette_convert_565_to_555.suppression_note: SUPPRESSION STARVES THE CALLER, same shape as llm_gfx_convert_pixels_565_to_555 but through the global `file_ptr` rather than a parameter (write-back at 0x0043c7f1). llm_tact_mission_load calls it and then immediately calls llm_tlo_shade_table_build_tact, which reads the converted palette bytes to build the shade table. Not `state` for the same reason: the palette lives in a heap buffer GetResourseFilePtr allocated, not at a declarable address.

llm_ui_set_draw_surface.why: Own body (0x004a8b73-0x004a8be7) is nine unconditional MOV stores of its own parameters into globals (DAT_005d8b38/3c/40/44/48/4c, DAT_00603af4, _G_LLM_UI_SURFACE_PTR, _G_LLM_UI_SURFACE_PITCH) -- no read-before-write on any of them. It then unconditionally CALLs llm_gfx_blit_rect_rows (0x004a8bdc -> 0x004a66cc), whose body I decompiled: a straight per-row `memcpy(dst,src,w*2)` loop over the just-set globals, with the row counter reset from DAT_005d8b4c each call -- no accumulator, no LUT-blend, no counter that survives across calls.
llm_ui_set_draw_surface.evidence_addr: 0x004a8bdc (CALL llm_gfx_blit_rect_rows) / 0x004a6725 (REP MOVSW memcpy body of the callee, no RMW)
llm_ui_set_draw_surface.twice_test: No accumulator anywhere in the chain -- every global is a plain store of the parameter, and the blit is a byte-for-byte memcpy driven entirely by those just-stored globals. Calling it twice with identical args (surface,pitch,x,y,clip*,src_bitmap) writes byte-identical globals and copies byte-identical pixel rows into the destination surface both times -- same final state, so it passes the twice-test. This mirrors the doctrine's own llm_tact_tile_overlay_refresh example (writes pixels into a display surface with no accumulator = idempotent = state, 'whatever its name suggests'), not the dashed-outline/scroll-fade counter-examples.

llm_view_set_size_mode.why: Body computes target w/h from size_mode, then at 0x0044e4e1 does CMP EAX,[EBP-0x24] against _G_LLM_VIEW_SIZE_MODE_CACHE; if equal it returns immediately (early-out, no further writes). Otherwise it calls llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution (0x0044e4f9, an already-gate-listed target), stores the applied mode into _G_LLM_VIEW_SIZE_MODE_CACHE (MOV [0x005d0c66],EAX at 0x0044e541), calls llm_map_set_zoom_scale(1.0,1.0) and game_SetEvent(HUD_REDRAW_ALL).
llm_view_set_size_mode.twice_test: NO -- the function has a built-in idempotency guard: mh_addrs.gen.h's own comment on _G_LLM_VIEW_SIZE_MODE_CACHE says 'it early-outs when this == the requested mode'. Call #1 (cache != size_mode) does the resize/cache-store/zoom-reset/event; call #2 with the SAME size_mode now hits cache==size_mode and returns immediately with NO further writes at all. Final state after 1 call == after 2 calls. The one non-idempotent-looking sub-call, llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution, is already on the existing gate list, so the exception rule applies regardless.
llm_view_set_size_mode.note: Entry conditionally owned by seams/video.cpp's D13b size-mode picker ([video] picker, default 0); effects_install.cpp defers the gate when that key is set. map_LoadPlanetFromDisk.why: Opens a fresh file handle (CALL utils_open_file @0x004481fb) and does ~35 sequential LZW_ReadCompressedFromFile calls (first at 0x00448222) that each UNCONDITIONALLY OVERWRITE a fixed-size shared buffer (units, buildings, tile_objects, _G_LLM_STRAT_ORDER_QUEUE, fog_of_war, passable, etc.) with bytes read from the file, then closes the file (0x004485e8) and calls a chain of deterministic setup functions (llm_map_setup_dimensions, llm_map_fog_of_war_recompute, llm_map_cam_set_col/row) that recompute state purely from what was just loaded. rsr_GetFileRealSize.why: Body itself only calls rsr_GetFileEntry(file_name,&pack) and, if found, reads prVar1->decompressed (0x004cf190) and returns it -- no writes of its own. rsr_GetFileEntry's body (0x004cefb7, read via ReVA) calls ToLower(fileName) which mutates the caller's string buffer in place, then linearly scans read-only pack/entry tables via utils_str_cmp and writes only the *rsr_out pack pointer (a value computed purely from the scan, not from rsr_out's prior contents). ToLower itself (0x004decdf) only stores a byte when it is currently uppercase ((c+0xbf)<0x1a test at 0x004decf1's guard) -- it is a fixed-point transform.

ToLower converges after one pass (an already-lowercase byte fails the uppercase test on pass 2, so it is left untouched), so file_name is bit-identical after 1 or 2 calls; the subsequent table scan and the returned `decompressed` size are then pure functions of that stabilized name and the (unwritten) pack tables -- same size both times. Independently confirmed by the project's own docs: src/mh_dll/mh/addr/mh_effects.gen.h:535 explicitly notes "time_GetCurrentTime (also reached) is a pure clock read, not itself part of the effect chain" for an unrelated gate target that reaches it, and src/mh_dll/libmh/lockstep/timekeeper.cpp:104 calls it as a plain `mh::call::time_GetCurrentTime` (an ordinary call-table entry, not a gate/replace).

A permanent false alarm is worse than no line. (2) It is `pure`, so a gate can never suppress it; its only contribution would be INV-4 effect-log recording -- and with 24 program-wide callers a single shadow window would blow the 64-event log, which DISABLES the INV-4 verdict for that window. Every instruction in both exit paths (LAB_004d1744: SUB EAX,EAX; LAB_004d176a: SBB EAX,EAX / OR AL,0x1) operates on registers only -- no memory store anywhere in the 0xa1-byte body.

w_sprintf.why: Formats varargs through the shared formatter __uprtf (CALL 0x004e08d7 at 0x004d033b) into the caller-supplied `dst` buffer, then NUL-terminates it (MOV word ptr [EDX],0x0 at 0x004d0346). Every write lands in the caller's own output buffer, computed purely from the read-only format string + varargs -- e.g. the game's own text-scratch buffer (G_TEXT_TMP) per numerous src/mh_dll/libmh/sim/*.h comments describing it as writing 'only the non-hashed text-scratch buffer'.

w_sprintf.gate_why: A GATE HERE WOULD CORRUPT 61 CALL SITES. w_sprintf is __cdecl and VARIADIC; its entry in dll_call_protos.json is a derived VARARGS SHAPE (`from_varargs_shape` id `vi`, one int32 vararg) recovered for ONE sim call site. A gate re-pushes exactly the parameters the shape names and calls the trampoline, so every caller passing a different number of varargs would have the rest read off the gate's own frame instead of its caller's. The shape is fit for CALLING the function from one known site; it is not a signature, and a hook over the entry needs a signature. Nothing is lost by leaving it ungated: it is `state` (it formats into a caller-supplied buffer), so a gate would never suppress it.
